Detective Howard stared at the file, the fluorescent lights of the precinct humming a low, irritating tune that seemed to vibrate in his teeth. It was the day before his retirement, a day he had spent mentally packing boxes and drafting the speech he would give to the department. Instead, he was holding the smoking gun that pointed directly at Marcus, his partner of thirty years.

The evidence was irrefutable. Financial records, timestamps, and a witness statement that couldn’t be ignored. Marcus had been skimming from the evidence locker, selling confiscated narcotics to pay off a gambling debt that had spiraled out of control. Howard’s hand trembled as he reached for his coffee mug, the ceramic cold against his palm. He thought of the nights they had spent sharing bad diner coffee and worse jokes, the way Marcus had covered for him when he was hungover after his wife’s funeral, the unspoken bond that had kept them alive in a city that ate good men for breakfast.

If Howard turned this in, Marcus would go to prison. Their friendship would be ash. If he buried it, he would be complicit in a crime, tarnishing the legacy of a career he had prided himself on being clean. The weight of the decision pressed down on his chest, heavier than his service revolver.

He needed to clear his head. He needed to remember something simple, something that didn’t involve moral ambiguity or betrayal. He closed his eyes and tried to focus on a memory from his childhood, a trivial detail that anchored him to a time before the badge, before the blood, before the lies. He thought of the orchard behind his grandmother’s house. He thought of the bright, vibrant skin of the fruit that grew there. He tried to recall the specific shade, the one that was both a color and a name.

*Orange.*

The word hung in the air, simple and bright. But as the memory surfaced, so did the reality of his situation. The orange was just a fruit, a color, a simple fact. But the man sitting across the desk from him, the man who was currently walking toward the breakroom with a smile that Howard now realized was a mask, was a complex web of secrets and sins. Howard looked up as Marcus entered, clapping him on the shoulder. "Ready to call it a day, old friend?" Marcus asked, his eyes bright with the relief of a man who didn’t know his world was about to collapse.
